gloss: equating; identifying with; treating as the same

definitions.gloss: equating; identifying with; treating as the same
definitions.explanation: Regarding two distinct things as identical or equivalent. Often used when pointing out that such an equation is problematic or incorrect.

examples.japanese: {二|ふた}つを{同一視|どういつし}してはいけない。
{愛国心|あいこくしん}と{国粋主義|こくすいしゅぎ}を{同一視|どういつし}するのは{間違|まちが}いだ。
examples.english: It's wrong to equate patriotism with ultranationalism.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}は{主人公|しゅじんこう}と{自分|じぶん}を{同一視|どういつし}しやすい。
examples.english: Children tend to identify themselves with the protagonist.

notes: Almost always used with する. Common patterns: AとBを{同一視|どういつし}する (to equate A with B), Aと{同一視|どういつし}される (to be identified with A). Often appears in argumentative or analytical writing when cautioning against treating different things as the same. Composed of {同一|どういつ} (identical, same) + {視|し} (viewing). Related: {同列|どうれつ}に{扱|あつか}う (to treat as equal), {一緒|いっしょ}にする (to lump together — more colloquial).
